title: Fuzzy Joins Using Neural Networks
text: First, must download model files ‘files versions’ pane model huggingface. run neural joins, need tokenizer files (tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json), model file ONNX format. huggingface repository several versions model, pick one called model_O3.onnx. version model optimizations make run faster, can still run CPU. Download files, put diretory (case, using _model/). model files set correctly, can load model memory, start generating emeddings. can load model new_inference_session function, takes path directory holding model tokenizer, also allows specify files hold model tokenizer differ defaults (‘model.onnx’ ‘tokenizer.json’, respectively). Now ready get going! can generate embeddings strings follows: join datasets based embeddings variables using familiar, dplyr-style syntax.
code: _model/ ├── model_O3.onnx ├── tokenizer_config.json └── tokenizer.json model <- new_inference_session("_model/", model = "model_O3.onnx") model ## An ORT inference session ## Using the model found at: ##   _model//model_O3.onnx  ## And the tokenizer found at: ##   _model//tokenizer.json embeddings <- generate_embeddings(model, c("the quick brown fox", "jumped over the lazy dog")) # only print first 5 dimensions embeddings[, 1:5] ##            [,1]      [,2]         [,3]      [,4]      [,5] ## [1,] 0.01882065 0.2252824 -0.004281675 0.2900443 0.2447263 ## [2,] 0.20537017 0.6361350  0.239320278 0.5308743 0.2489903 a <- data.frame(                name_1 =                    c("JP Morgan Chase",                      "he was sad",                      "he is happy",                      "Bank of America",                      "the lazy dog was jumped over by the quick brown fox"                    )                ) b <- data.frame(                 name_2 =                     c("JP Morgan",                       "the man was morose",                       "the man was smiling",                       "Bank of America",                       "the quick brown fox vaulted over the sleeping dog")                ) neural_inner_join(a,b, model, by = c('name_1' = 'name_2'), radius = .5) ## # A tibble: 5 × 2 ##   name_1                                              name_2                     ##   <chr>                                               <chr>                      ## 1 JP Morgan Chase                                     JP Morgan                  ## 2 he was sad                                          the man was morose         ## 3 he is happy                                         the man was smiling        ## 4 Bank of America                                     Bank of America            ## 5 the lazy dog was jumped over by the quick brown fox the quick brown fox vault…
